lead: Interchangeable parts need agreed sizes. Preferred numbers fix the standard sizes of shafts, holes, bolts and stock so factories make few variants. Fits and tolerances fix how much a part may vary and how tightly a shaft must sit in a hole. A 25 mm shaft made in one shop must enter a 25 mm hole made in another, with the planned clearance or grip. This chapter gives the vocabulary, the ISO shorthand such as H7/g6, and the cost trade-off behind every tolerance on a drawing.
prereq: You need 1.1 and 1.2 for function and material choice.

blocks.text: Factories make few sizes and buy stock in bulk. Preferred numbers are the agreed sizes. They are geometric series: each term is the previous term times a fixed ratio. R5 has 5 steps per decade, R10 has 10, R20 has 20 and R40 has 40. One decade runs from 10 to 100, or 1 to 10, and repeats by powers of ten.

blocks.where: q is the step ratio; n is 5, 10, 20 or 40 for R5, R10, R20 or R40; i = 0, 1, ..., n; k is the decade (..., −1, 0, 1, ...); N_i is the unrounded preferred number, later rounded to the standard value.

blocks.text: R5 ratio is about 1.585; R10 ratio is about 1.259. The calculated values are rounded to familiar numbers: 10, 12.5, 16, 20, 25, 31.5, 40, 50, 63, 80. The figure shows one decade.

Geometric spacing gives equal relative steps. A 10 mm shaft grows by 2.5 mm in R10; a 100 mm shaft grows by 25 mm. Small parts get fine choices, large parts get coarse choices, and one series covers both. Use preferred numbers for diameters, lengths, power ratings and capacities. A 25 mm shaft is preferred; 24.8 mm is not.

sections.h3: Basic size, limits, tolerance and allowance

blocks.text: Basic size D is the nominal size on the drawing, 25 mm in the example. The actual size is what the micrometer reads. No machinist can hit D exactly at affordable cost, so the drawing gives two limits: upper limit UL and lower limit LL.

blocks.where: T is the tolerance in mm; UL is the upper limit in mm; LL is the lower limit in mm.

blocks.text: Some syllabi call tolerance the permissible variation. A size written 25 ±0.010 mm has UL = 25.010 mm, LL = 24.990 mm and T = 0.020 mm. Tolerance is the full band, not the plus-or-minus number.
Deviation is a limit minus the basic size. The hole lower deviation EI = LL_hole − D. The shaft upper deviation es = UL_shaft − D. These signed deviations are what ISO letters and numbers encode.

blocks.where: A is the allowance in mm; LL_hole is the hole lower limit; UL_shaft is the shaft upper limit. Positive A means clearance at the tightest assembly; negative A means interference.

blocks.text: Allowance is the planned minimum clearance or maximum interference. It is fixed by the limits. Clearance is the actual gap in one assembled pair, and it can range from minimum to maximum.

Three fits describe the tolerance zones. In a clearance fit the hole is always larger than the shaft, so minimum clearance is positive. In an interference fit the shaft is always larger, so there is negative clearance, called interference. In a transition fit the zones overlap: a given pair may have a small clearance or a small interference.

Hole-basis system: the hole lower deviation is zero, written H. The basic size is the hole minimum. The shaft letter and grade set the fit. Shaft-basis system: the shaft upper deviation is zero, written h, and the hole is varied. Uppercase letters are holes; lowercase letters are shafts. H7/g6 is hole-basis; h6/G7 is shaft-basis.

ISO IT grades number the tolerance width. Smaller grade number means tighter tolerance. IT01 to IT18 cover the range. General machinery commonly uses IT7 for holes and IT6 for shafts, giving fits such as H7/g6.
Use H7/g6 for a sliding spigot, H7/h6 for easy location, H7/k6 for a keyed or pinned joint, and H7/p6 for a press fit. Bearing and gear fits are chosen from catalogue tables; see Unit 5 and Unit 7.
Every dimension in an assembly adds its tolerance to the final gap. In the worst case all parts sit at their extreme limits:

blocks.where: T_stack is the worst-case assembly tolerance in mm; T_i is the tolerance of part i in mm; the sum runs over all parts in the chain.

blocks.text: If the errors are independent, the statistical stack is T_stat = √(Σ T_i²). The statistical value is smaller because all errors rarely reach their limits together.

Cost rises steeply as tolerance tightens. A 0.1 mm band may come from ordinary turning. A 0.01 mm band needs grinding and inspection. A 0.001 mm band needs lapping, temperature control and a skilled operator. The drawing should give the loosest tolerance that still works, and tight tolerances only on functional dimensions.
Stack the tolerances before release. A chain of five parts, each ±0.02 mm, gives ±0.10 mm worst case. If the gap needs ±0.05 mm, either tighten the chain or use selective assembly.

examples.question: A nominal 25 mm hole has limits 25.000 mm and 25.021 mm. The mating shaft has limits 24.980 mm and 24.993 mm. Find the hole tolerance, shaft tolerance, allowance, maximum clearance and minimum clearance. Name the fit and its ISO designation.
steps: Hole tolerance T_h = UL_h − LL_h = 25.021 − 25.000 = 0.021 mm.
Shaft tolerance T_s = UL_s − LL_s = 24.993 − 24.980 = 0.013 mm.
Allowance A = LL_h − UL_s = 25.000 − 24.993 = +0.007 mm. Positive A means clearance at the tightest assembly.

Both extremes are positive, so the fit is a clearance fit. The hole lower limit equals the basic size 25.000 mm, so the hole is H. Hole tolerance 0.021 mm is IT7 at 25 mm, so the hole is H7. Shaft deviations are es = 24.993 − 25.000 = −0.007 mm and ei = 24.980 − 25.000 = −0.020 mm, which is g6. The fit is H7/g6.
examples.answer: Hole tolerance 0.021 mm, shaft tolerance 0.013 mm, allowance 0.007 mm, maximum clearance 0.041 mm, minimum clearance 0.007 mm; the fit is a clearance fit, H7/g6.
examples.check:
hole_max = 25.021
hole_min = 25.000
shaft_max = 24.993
shaft_min = 24.980
hole_tol = round(hole_max - hole_min, 3)
shaft_tol = round(shaft_max - shaft_min, 3)
allowance = round(hole_min - shaft_max, 3)
max_clearance = round(hole_max - shaft_min, 3)
min_clearance = round(hole_min - shaft_max, 3)
print(hole_tol)
print(shaft_tol)
print(allowance)
print(max_clearance)
print(min_clearance)

traps: Allowance is not the same as clearance. Allowance is the planned minimum clearance or maximum interference from the limits; clearance is the actual gap in one assembled pair.
Tolerance is the full band, not the plus-or-minus value. A size 25 ±0.010 mm has tolerance 0.020 mm, not 0.010 mm.
Hole-basis and shaft-basis look alike in writing. H7/g6 is hole-basis because H is capital. h6/G7 is shaft-basis because h is small. Capital letters always mean holes.
Minimum clearance uses the smallest hole and the largest shaft. Maximum clearance uses the largest hole and the smallest shaft. Reversing them gives a wrong sign.
A smaller IT number is a tighter tolerance. IT6 is tighter than IT8, not looser.

quiz.q: What does the label R10 mean in a preferred-number series?
quiz.a: A geometric series with 10 steps per decade; the step ratio is 10^(1/10) ≈ 1.259.

quiz.q: Why are preferred numbers geometric rather than arithmetic?
quiz.a: Geometric steps give equal relative change. A small part gets a small absolute step and a large part gets a large absolute step, so one series works over a wide range.

quiz.q: A 40 mm hole has limits 40.000 mm and 40.025 mm. The shaft has limits 39.975 mm and 39.991 mm. Find maximum clearance, minimum clearance and the fit type.
quiz.a: Maximum clearance = 40.025 − 39.975 = 0.050 mm. Minimum clearance = 40.000 − 39.991 = 0.009 mm. Both are positive, so it is a clearance fit.

quiz.q: A drawing changes from H7/g6 to H7/p6 at the same basic size. What changes on the shop floor?
quiz.a: H7/g6 is a clearance fit, so the parts slide together. H7/p6 is an interference fit, so assembly needs a press or shrink fit, the hub carries hoop stress, and disassembly may damage surfaces.

quiz.q: Five dimensions in a stack each have tolerance 0.020 mm. Find the worst-case stack tolerance. Why is the statistical estimate smaller?
quiz.a: Worst case = 5 × 0.020 = 0.100 mm. Statistical root-sum-square = √(5 × 0.020²) ≈ 0.045 mm, because independent errors rarely all sit at their limits together.

quiz.q: State the difference between allowance and clearance.
quiz.a: Allowance is the planned minimum clearance or maximum interference from the limits. Clearance is the actual gap for one produced pair and varies between minimum and maximum clearance.

quiz.q: Name the three classes of fit.
In H7/g6, which letter is the hole and which is the shaft? What does the capital letter tell you?
quiz.a: H is the hole and g is the shaft. A capital letter is the hole; lowercase is the shaft. H means the hole lower deviation is zero, so it is hole-basis.

beyond: Not for the exam. On real drawings you will meet ISO 286 limit tables, geometric dimensioning and tolerancing callouts, and statistical tolerance analysis. Selective assembly and Monte Carlo tolerance simulation are used where a stack is too tight for normal production. Additive manufacturing changes the cost curve for small batches, but the limit-and-fit logic stays. Search next for ISO 286, tolerance stack-up analysis and GD&T position tolerance.
